title: A day in my life
stereotype: the 'day in the life' of doing very little: an influencer documents a gruelling day of an iced coffee, one email and a pilates class, then complains about being exhausted
observation: Influencers narrate a day of almost nothing as if it were gruelling, and a dog's day is genuinely nothing, so the two match beat for beat
stupid_premise: Gary, who has done nothing all day, documents it as a demanding wellness-and-productivity schedule and is visibly drained by it
cruel_payoff: Doug, who watched the whole day, stares into the lens on 'honestly so drained' and again as Gary sleep-runs through his 'reset'
dog_does: under "a day in my life": Gary wakes on an unmade bed, stretches front legs, yawns; under "iced coffee run": Gary in the passenger seat, ears blowing, grins at the lens; under "grabbing my order": Gary noses into a takeaway paper bag on the kitchen floor; under "setting up my workspace": Gary nose-dives into the sofa throw and stays face-down; under "answered one email": Gary sitting on the rug nods off and slides flat; under "meal prep": Gary buries a treat on bare tile; it stays in plain sight; under "hydration": Gary drinks noisily from his water bowl, water slopping onto the floor; under "pilates": Gary creeps on his elbows to Doug's bowl; under "stretching it out": Gary belly-up against the sofa, one huge stretch, goes limp; under "getting my steps in": Gary trots three laps of the rug chasing nothing, then flops; under "honestly so drained": Gary yawns hugely while Doug stares into the lens; under "need a reset tbh": Gary paddles in his sleep while Doug stares
caption: Some days you just have to protect your energy.
beats_live: F43 parodies a work-from-home job with a working dog's routine; this parodies the lifestyle influencer whose day has no job in it at all, and its payoff is the second dog's judgement, which F43 never had
why_new: the exhausted lifestyle diary, not a work routine or a morning routine

title: I am obsessed
stereotype: the 'obsessed' product push: an influencer claims months of use of a product that is clearly brand new, with 'literally life-changing' and 'run, don't walk'
observation: Sponsored creators rave about a product with buzzwords that would fit any product, and the product always turns out to be about them
stupid_premise: Gary raves about a blanket in full influencer voice, burrowing, stretching and dozing on it
cruel_payoff: the product he is obsessed with is a blanket covered in paintings of his own face
dog_does: under "ok I am obsessed": Gary nose-dives into the throw; under "unboxing": Gary tears at a delivery box on the hallway floor, cardboard flying; under "the texture": Gary circles three times and kneads a blanket before lying down; under "been using it for months": Gary belly-up, one huge stretch, limp; under "obsessed with the fit": Gary rolls on his back on the blanket, legs wiggling; under "literally life-changing": Gary nods off sitting and slides flat; under "my partner wants one": Doug tries to step onto the blanket; Gary lifts his lip without moving; under "not sharing": Gary lies over his treat, squinting at the lens; under "run, don't walk": Gary yawns; Doug stares; under "it is me": the store's own painted blanket of Gary, held 3 s
caption: Not sponsored. He is the product.
beats_live: F34 is a group chat roasting a dog who put his face on Mom's gift; this is the dog doing the sponsored rave himself in the influencer format, so the vanity is his own voice, not his friends' roast
why_new: the sponsored product push, ending on the real gift

title: Yes, we're that couple
stereotype: the over-performed relationship: a couple films scripted affection, date nights and 'communication is key', then pushes their joint podcast
observation: Couple accounts perform closeness so hard it reads as a hostage video
stupid_premise: Gary and Doug present themselves as relationship goals while doing what dogs actually do to each other
cruel_payoff: date night is Gary sniffing Doug's rear while he eats, 'we share everything' is Gary creeping onto Doug's dinner, and 'communication is key' is a yawn in Doug's face

title: Please respect the set
stereotype: main character syndrome while filming: a creator sets up a tripod for a wellness flow and gets visibly annoyed when regular people walk through the background of the shot
observation: Creators who film in shared spaces treat everyone else as an intrusion into their content
stupid_premise: Gary is filming his morning yoga flow on a purple mat in the backyard and Doug keeps wandering into the shot
cruel_payoff: Doug does not just walk through: he lies down on the mat, half on Gary, and becomes the content; Gary ends deadpan under Doug's chin
dog_does: under "filming my morning flow": Gary play-bows on the mat; Doug stands behind, looking at the lens; under "this is a closed set": Doug sniffs a hole behind the mat and trots off; under "please respect the craft": Doug digs right behind the mat, dirt flying; under "back in flow": Gary alone on the mat again; under "take two": Doug shakes off water right beside the mat; under "take five": Doug zooms through the back of the shot; under "he is now in the content": Doug lies down half on Gary; under "collab I did not approve": Doug's chin on Gary's back; Gary stares
words: he is now in the content
caption: Some people have no respect for the craft.
beats_live: V005 parodies the gym-era self-improvement arc; this parodies the creator who films in public and is annoyed by bystanders, and the joke is the second dog invading the shot, not the workout
why_new: the annoyed creator and the bystander who walks into the shot
